title: The Geometry of Polycons and a Counterexample to Wachspress' Conjecture
summary: Polycons, initially introduced by Wachspress in 1975 as a tool in finite element methods, are generalizations of polygons in that they allow conic boundary components. We are interested in the adjoint curve of a given polycon, i.e. the unique curve of minimal degree vanishing in the so-called residual arrangement. It was conjectured by Wachspress that under some regularity assumptions this curve does not vanish in the interior of its defining polycon.
